description: Blind search for strictly periodic variation in ZTF DR light curves of Gaia DR3 quasar candidates (G <= 19, classifier probability >= 0.9, parallax S/N <= 3, proper motion <= 3 mas/yr) in nested HEALPix cell order 2, pixel 100. Every object gets a decoy twin; 40% get a planted signal; all are sealed and analysed alike. Promotion rule, fixed here: probability <= 0.001 after population recalibration, no vetting gate failed, and still <= 0.001 when recalibrated with 20,000 fresh simulated nulls. Disclosed beforehand: (1) the code was developed on simulations only; (2) an engineering check of the real-data path used 47 quasars in order-4 pixel 600, which is not in this sample, and led to three changes made before this registration: the search now starts at 40-day periods to stay clear of the lunar month, all ZTF light-curve fragments are used, and the season rule became a time-span rule; (3) PG 1302-102, which lies in this cell, was examined in the research phase with an earlier, different method. Whatever the outcome, including nothing, it will be recorded here.

description:
Control objects, searched one at a time with the registered periodicity configuration and the same gates.

Chosen before looking at their results with this code:

* PG 1553+113 (4FGL J1555.7+1111): a blazar with a published claim of a roughly 2.2-year cycle in Fermi-LAT
  gamma rays. A positive control of the "famous candidate" kind: the question is not whether the claim is
  right but what this pipeline says when given the same public data.
* KIC 8462852 (Boyajian's star): deep, irregular dips in Kepler photometry. A strange object that is not known
  to be periodic: the pipeline should not turn strangeness into a period.

Usage: python run_controls.py register | run SEARCH_ID

config.rule: an object is a hit if the test reports discrete levels at probability <= alpha; the same test runs on each object's decoy twin under hidden labels
config.test: decode.symbolise.discreteness_test on the merged nightly light curve, default settings (up to 6 levels, at least 8 error bars apart, at most 10% of points off-level, 200 red-noise decoys)

description:
A second blind search on the same quasars: does any light curve sit on discrete levels?

A source whose brightness is keyed between a few fixed levels is the simplest coded signal a slowly sampled
light curve could carry. The test is strict (see `stargazer.decode.symbolise`): nearly every nightly point
must lie within its error bar of one of a few levels that are at least eight error bars apart, and red noise
simulated from the object's own fit must almost never look as discrete. Every object's decoy twin (a
simulation of its fitted red noise at its own sampling) is put through the same test under hidden labels, so
the false-alarm count is measured.

Usage: python run_levels.py register | run SEARCH_ID [engineering]

hypothesis: quasar-ztf-gaia-pix2-100: gaia:3613794004069753472 is periodic at 79.9 d

text: Follow-up of the promoted object: Gaia DR3 lists it as an RR Lyrae star (RRab, period 0.49624 d); unbinned ZTF data give 0.49622 d; the 79.9-day cycle is the alias of that pulsation under nightly sampling. Disposition: known natural class.

description:
Do the bursts of two repeating fast radio bursts keep time?

Two questions per source, each answered against surrogates that keep the burst rate and its slow changes and
destroy only fine timing (see `stargazer.detect.intervals`):

* clock: do the arrival times fall on the ticks of a regular clock, with some ticks empty?
* spacing: are the gaps between bursts whole multiples of one unit?

Sources, chosen before looking at their timing with this code:

* FRB 20220912A, 696 bursts in 68 Nançay scans, moved to the Solar System barycentre, with the scan log as
  exposure;
* FRB 20220529, 643 FAST bursts, already barycentric, without exposure information.

Four tests in all. A test is a hit if its probability is at or below 0.01 / 4 (Bonferroni over the four),
with 999 surrogates each. Period range: the default of the tests, a tenth of the median gap to twice it.
FRB 20180916B is left out: its compiled observing windows are incomplete, and a timing test without honest
exposure would not mean much.

Usage: python run_timing.py register | run SEARCH_ID | engineering
